evidence.claim: The cardholder confirmed the $77.07 card-present purchase in region 444 on 2016-12-04 and also confirmed the purchases in regions 485 and 203, stating they were running errands in the area.
Region 444 is not new for this card: 10 prior transactions in that region in the 180-day baseline, new_region_for_card = false, so the out_of_region_use (clone) pattern does not apply.
Amount $77.07 is 0.66x the card's 180-day mean of $117.02 (z = -0.34), well under the $845.01 max across 358 transactions; channel in_person and product W each cover 99.4% of history.

All 9 transactions in the 3-4 December window are card-present product W in familiar regions (433, 204, 191, 485, 203, 444); 0 online transactions, no card-testing runs, no just-under-$500 runs, no new device and no proxy.
No rare shared device profiles and no cards linked by a rare device for this card (rare_shared_devices_total = 0), so no shared-origin ring evidence.
Region 444 shows 8 newcomer cards in 7 days with 6 having confirmed fraud history (75% vs 10% base rate), but C12382-K1 is not among the newcomers, so the cluster does not implicate this card.

Prior confirmed-fraud cases on this same card all involved a genuinely new billing region (CC-1066, CC-3587, CC-2964) or a new online device (CC-1673); neither condition holds for transaction 3514030.
Semantically similar closed cases with high model scores on familiar regional activity were cleared after the cardholder confirmed (CC-4349 at 0.93, CC-1149 at 0.82).
Policy R3 directs CLOSE_NO_FRAUD when the customer confirms the transaction, with the confirmation noted in the case file.

case.summary: Alert HHG-001 was raised purely by a 0.61 model score on transaction 3514030 ($77.07, card-present, region 444). Every structural signal points to normal behaviour for card C12382-K1: the amount is below the card's mean, the channel and product match 99.4% of 358 baseline transactions, and region 444 already carries 10 prior transactions on this card, so this is not out-of-region use. The 3-4 December window is an unbroken sequence of ordinary in-person purchases in the cardholder's usual regions with no online activity, no new device, and no rare shared device links. The cardholder has confirmed the flagged purchase and the neighbouring ones. Under policy R3 the alert should be closed as no fraud, with the confirmation recorded; the region 444 newcomer cluster is noted but does not involve this card.
